title: Statement of Concern Related to Certain Minerals Supply Chains from Rwanda and Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo Contributing to the Ongoing Conflict

notes: Uploaded Oct 2026, but the document shows no exact date. It confirms that the Washington Accords comprise the 27 Jun 2025 peace agreement plus the REIF, and it describes $25M of FY2026 minerals programming (traceable certification for artisanal mining).

title: Treasury Sanctions Rwandan Gold Refinery and Network Enabling Illicit Conflict Minerals Trade
notes: Date confirmed by the OFAC recent-actions link (20260625). The release also says a March 2026 mine-shaft collapse at Rubaya killed over 200 people. That conflicts with the 'Jan 2026, at least 227' figure in RWANDA_CASE.md, which belongs to the impacts layer (see run notes).

title: Treasury Sanctions Rwandan Ministry of Defence and Financial Institution Supporting M23
paragraph_or_page: Sections 'The Rwandan Ministry of Defence' and 'Zigama'
notes: Date confirmed by the OFAC recent-actions link (20261028). The release notes that on 12 Oct 2026 the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation announced itself as the AFC's successor.

title: The United States Announces Sanctions in Response to Rwanda's Destabilizing Activities in Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo
publisher: US Department of State, Office of the Spokesman (Tommy Pigott)
notes: Contains the call for partners and the private sector to examine their supply chains, with reference to gold and coltan areas under M23 control including Rubaya. This is a sentence in a press statement, not a standalone business advisory.

title: ITSCI comments on recent Global Witness investigation
paragraph_or_page: Paragraph on actions taken since start of 2025
notes: Names African Panther Resources Ltd (suspended 16 Mar 2025) and Sunrise Metal Company Ltd (suspended 16 Apr 2025) for insufficient evidence of due diligence.

title: Quarterly membership update Q4 2025
notes: Space Mining Ltd suspended 13 Oct 2025; Philbert Trading Minerals Ltd suspended 12 Nov 2025. The other suspensions on 16 Oct 2025 (DFSA Mining Congo, Metachem, MTALX, NPM Silmet, SAKIMA, TMT, Vin Metal Synergies, Yinchuan Kinfintra) appear to be non-Rwandan or non-exporter members, and some are likely for fee non-payment. Do not count them as Rwandan coltan exporters without checking.

title: ITSCI statement: Shifts in tantalum mineral flows from the Great Lakes Region
notes: Says four Rwandan exporters were suspended in 2025 up to that date.

title: ITSCI response to Global Witness report on Rwanda's coltan
notes: Four GW-named exporters suspended in 2025 or 2026, plus a fifth (not GW-named) suspended in 2026. High-level incidents are open on three more GW-named exporters and on one other. The 5th exporter is not named.

title: Statement: 3T mineral flows from the Great Lakes Region (context of UN GoE 2025 final report)
notes: Says six local exporters suspended so far. Also says the UN GoE final report was published 5 Jun 2026 (para 223, p.40 cited).

title: Who buys Rwanda's smuggled coltan?
paragraph_or_page: Sections on ITSCI and Better Mining; company responses
notes: States six coltan exporters suspended or expelled by ITSCI since 2024. Space Mining and Philbert are now with Better Mining, and Sunrise is onboarding. GW says APR's suspension was lifted. Published date taken from DATA_SOURCES.md ('updated 18 June 2026'), not from the extract.

title: Regulation (EU) 2025/1561 amending Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 as regards battery due diligence obligations

title: Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 concerning batteries and waste batteries
publisher: EUR-Lex / Official Journal of the EU
notes: Annex X point 1 lists cobalt, natural graphite, lithium and nickel (and their compounds) only. The Commission may amend the list, including in light of changes to Regulation 2017/821. Published date is the OJ publication date from general knowledge and was not seen in the extract.

title: Rwanda Regrets One-Sided Sanctions
publisher: Republic of Rwanda, Office of the Government Spokesperson
notes: Response to OFAC sb0411. It does not literally say 'we do not support M23'. Instead it calls the sanctions one-sided and blames DRC/FDLR violations.

title: US imposes sanctions on Rwanda's defense ministry over Congo conflict
notes: Reports that Rwanda denies backing the rebels (now Refoundation of the Nation, formerly AFC-M23). Quotes government spokesperson Yolande Makolo saying the DRC's FDLR commitments are unmet. No primary gov.rw text for this date was found.

title: DR Congo: More than 200 killed in mine collapse
notes: Published date approximate (article covers the 28 Jan collapse and the governor's visit the following Friday). Gives >200 from the spokesman of the M23-appointed governor.

title: Hundreds Killed in Rubaya Mine Collapse Amidst DRC's Mineral War
notes: Published about one week after 28 Jan 2026 (exact date not captured). Site: Luwowo, Gasasa. M23-installed governor's spokesman: >200 provisional; a rescuer: >430 bodies recovered. Quotes the DRC government statement (condolences; 112-125 t of coltan extracted monthly, all to Rwanda).

title: La RD Congo évoque 'plus de 200 morts, dont 70 enfants mineurs' dans un éboulement à Rubaya
notes: Quotes a DRC Ministry of Mines communiqué of 4 Mar 2026 on the SECOND landslide (3 Mar 2026, Gasasa): >200 dead, ~70 minors. Recaps 28 Jan: local authorities said 200; Masisi civil society said nearer 400.

title: RDC : Plus de 200 morts et des disparus dans un nouvel éboulement minier à Rubaya
notes: Published early Mar 2026. DRC Mines Minister Louis Watum Kabamba: >200 dead, including children, in the 3 Mar 2026 collapse (Kasasa site). States the 28 Jan collapse killed >200 according to M23 authorities.

title: The 28 January 2026 landslide at the Rubaya coltan mine complex in the Democratic Republic of Congo
notes: Secondary: cites Discovery Alert for 'at least 227 killed, 20 injured' and gives the approximate landslide location as -1.55938, 28.88349. Notes an earlier landslide on 19 Jun 2025 with >300 reported dead.

title: Gasabo Gold Refinery LTD - OpenSanctions entity (incl. EU listing text)
publisher: OpenSanctions (aggregating EU FSF / Council of the EU, OFAC)
notes: Carries the EU statement of reasons (French): began refining 1 Jun 2022 after Aldango Gold Refinery closed; Rwanda's only gold refinery. EU listing 17 Mar 2025. Incorporation 26 May 2022 (company no. 120323055). For citation, prefer the Official Journal entry; OpenSanctions is an aggregator.

title: UAE Cooperation
publisher: Embassy of the Republic of Rwanda in the UAE (gov.rw)
notes: UAE is Rwanda's leading trade partner; main exports to the UAE include gold, coltan and horticulture. No gold-specific volumes.

notes: UAE took 63.9% of Rwanda's formal goods exports in 2024 (US$1.55bn), up from 56.9% in 2023. Not broken down by commodity.

notes: Area of influence built from ACLED plus media. Latest asset is an animated map covering Jan-May 2026 (uploaded 2026/06). AOI shapefiles exist internally (scale 1:1,500,000, ±10 km), but no public download link is shown. IPIS warns they must not be used to decide whether a specific village or mine is under M23 control.
